name: Daptomycin
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Daptomycin is excreted mainly by the kidneys (about 78% of a dose in urine). The US label keeps the usual once-daily mg/kg dose down to a creatinine clearance (CrCl) of 30 mL/min and gives the same mg/kg dose every 48 hours below 30, including hemodialysis (after the session) and CAPD. Creatine phosphokinase (CPK) and kidney function need checking more often than weekly in kidney impairment, and efficacy was lower in moderate kidney impairment.
kidney_function_basis: Label uses CrCl (mL/min; Cockcroft–Gault with actual body weight); cut-off 30.
chip: CrCl <30, HD, CAPD: dose every 48 h

bands.recommendation: Usual dose: 4 mg/kg (complicated skin infections) or 6 mg/kg (S. aureus bloodstream infection) once every 24 hours (label: CrCl 30 or more).
Usual dose every 24 hours (CrCl 30 or more). Caution: lower clinical success in adults with CrCl 30 to <50 in trials; monitor CPK and kidney function more often than weekly (label 5.2, 5.10).
CrCl <30: 4 mg/kg (complicated skin infections) or 6 mg/kg (S. aureus bloodstream infection) once every 48 hours (label).
CrCl <30: 4 mg/kg (complicated skin infections) or 6 mg/kg (S. aureus bloodstream infection) once every 48 hours (label).

hd: 4 mg/kg (complicated skin infections) or 6 mg/kg (S. aureus bloodstream infection) once every 48 hours (label). Give after hemodialysis on dialysis days when possible. Literature option (not label): thrice-weekly after each session, 6, 6 and 9 mg/kg for most infections, or 8, 8 and 12 mg/kg for Staphylococcus aureus; optimal dosing for vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium is unclear and no regimen is recommended (Tsai 2025). These regimens are not weight-adjusted and come mostly from small pharmacokinetic studies; confirm the actual last and next session before each dose. See the site guide Antibiotic Stewardship in Hemodialysis (/guides/antibiotic-stewardship-dialysis.html).
pd: CAPD: 4 mg/kg (complicated skin infections) or 6 mg/kg (S. aureus bloodstream infection) once every 48 hours (label).
crrt: Not in label. Li 2020 (Table 3): CVVHD dialysate rate above 30 mL/kg/h, 6 mg/kg every 24 hours; CVVHDF combined flow above 30 mL/kg/h, 6 to 8 mg/kg every 24 hours; watch for toxicity with higher doses.
dialyzable: Slowly: about 15% of a dose removed over 4 hours of hemodialysis and 11% over 48 hours of peritoneal dialysis; high-flux membranes may remove more (label). Protein binding 90% to 93%.
monitoring: CPK weekly, and more often in kidney impairment or with statins; kidney function; muscle pain or weakness; eosinophilic pneumonia; neuropathy (label). Daptomycin can falsely prolong PT/INR with some reagents (label).

pediatric.usual_dose: Complicated skin infections, once every 24 hours: 12–17 years 5 mg/kg; 7–11 years 7 mg/kg; 2–6 years 9 mg/kg; 1 to <2 years 10 mg/kg. S. aureus bacteremia: 12–17 years 7 mg/kg; 7–11 years 9 mg/kg; 1–6 years 12 mg/kg (label).
